Study the motion of interconnected rigid bodies, analyze the forces and torques acting on them, and design mechanisms to accomplish prescribed tasks.

These lectures follow the chapter sequence of *Kinematics and Machine Dynamics: A Geometric Approach to the Motion of Interconnected Rigid Bodies*, the notes compiled by Aykut C. Satici for his Boise State University course.

## Syllabus

[Fall 2021 syllabus (PDF)](resources/syllabus-fall2021.pdf) for ME 380 at Boise State University. This is the syllabus from the most recent offering represented in these course materials.

## Background and references

The course uses calculus, vectors and matrices, and introductory engineering mechanics. The compiled notes include appendices on linear algebra, differentiation of vectors, and nonlinear systems.

The primary reference is Satici's compiled course notes (Fall 2020 version). Chapter 1 follows Charles E. Wilson and J. Peter Sadler, *Kinematics and Dynamics of Machinery*, Pearson New International Edition (2013). Chapter 5 follows Richard M. Murray, Zexiang Li, and S. Shankar Sastry, *A Mathematical Introduction to Robotic Manipulation*. Chapters 6–10 draw on the compiled notes and Thomas R. Kane and David A. Levinson, *Dynamics: Theory and Applications* (1985). Each deck includes its references.

## Reference books

- Thomas R. Kane and David A. Levinson, [*Dynamics: Theory and Applications* (PDF)](https://ecommons.cornell.edu/bitstream/1813/638/10/Dynamics-Theory_opt.pdf).
- Richard M. Murray, Zexiang Li, and S. Shankar Sastry, [*A Mathematical Introduction to Robotic Manipulation*](https://murray.cds.caltech.edu/MLS_second_edition). The linked page contains information about the second edition.

Chapter 11 follows David E. Stewart, [“Rigid-Body Dynamics with Friction and Impact”](https://doi.org/10.1137/S0036144599360110), *SIAM Review* 42(1), 3–39 (2000).

:::
